corrected_value.title: Common variants on 9q22.33 and 14q13.3 predispose to thyroid cancer in European populations.

decision.quote: We confirmed the well-known association with DTC of the 9q22.31 region that includes the FOXE1 gene ( 9–12 ). In this independent and separate case–control study conducted in Germany, we replicated associations with PTC risk that we reported previously in SERPINA5 ( 21 ) and FTO ( 17 ) genes. Other candidate variants in EVPL , TICAM1 and SCARB1 previously identified ( 17 , 21 ) were also associated with PTC risk. We found several new associations between SNPs in SERPINA5 , FTO , TICAM1 and HSPA6 genes, and risk of FTC. In contrast to several studies, we did not observe associations for NKX2-1 SNPs ( 9 , 25 , 26 ).
decision.reason: The German case-control study explicitly selected three SNPs in FOXE1 (9q22.33, including rs965513) and two SNPs in NKX2-1 (14q13.3) for empirical validation from reference 9 (Gudmundsson et al., 2009) and tested them in 552 DTC cases and 752 controls (Materials and methods; Results Table 2; Discussion), confirming the FOXE1 association while not observing the NKX2-1 association. The sole shipped row (input_row_index 84, Neta et al., 2011, 10.1093/carcin/bgr100, reference 16) is a distinct US NCI i-Select candidate-gene study of genomic integrity variants (such as HDAC4), and sibling targets 1–3 and 5–6 are separate empirical studies in different populations or gene pathways, so report equivalence does not apply.

decision.reason: The authors selected FOXE1 SNPs from references 9–12 for empirical validation (Materials and methods), specifically genotyped and retested rs1867277 (the exact functional FOXE1 variant reported by reference 12, Landa et al., 2009) in the German case-control sample (Results Table 2: PTC P = 0.0009, DTC P = 0.0018), and confirmed the FOXE1 association in the Discussion. The sole shipped row (input_row_index 84, Neta et al., 2011, 10.1093/carcin/bgr100, reference 16) is a different study on genomic integrity genes, and reference 12 is an independent candidate-gene study distinct from sibling targets 0, 1, 2, 5, and 6.

corrected_value.title: Common obesity-related genetic variants and papillary thyroid cancer risk.

decision.quote: In this independent and separate case–control study conducted in Germany, we replicated associations with PTC risk that we reported previously in SERPINA5 ( 21 ) and FTO ( 17 ) genes. Other candidate variants in EVPL , TICAM1 and SCARB1 previously identified ( 17 , 21 ) were also associated with PTC risk.
decision.reason: The main objective of the study was to replicate findings from the NCI rare cancer i-Select papers (16–21), specifically adding SNPs in FTO and SCARB1 for validation (Introduction; Materials and methods), empirically testing them in the German sample (Results Table 2: FTO rs8047395 and SCARB1 rs11057820), and explicitly confirming the PTC associations from reference 17 (Kitahara et al., 2012). Although reference 17 and shipped row 84 (Neta et al., 2011, 10.1093/carcin/bgr100, reference 16) both used the NCI i-Select platform, they are separate publications analyzing different candidate gene pathways and reporting distinct genetic findings (obesity-related variants in FTO/SCARB1 versus genomic integrity variants such as HDAC4), so report equivalence does not apply.

corrected_value.title: Common genetic variants in the 8q24 region and risk of papillary thyroid cancer.

decision.quote: We also did not replicate earlier findings on the associations with HDAC4 ( 16 ) and the 8q24 region SNPs for PTC ( 18 ).
decision.reason: The authors explicitly selected SNPs in the 8q24 region with high priors from the NCI i-Select study (reference 18, Neta et al., 2012) for validation in the German case-control sample (Introduction; Materials and methods) and explicitly reported that the earlier findings on 8q24 region SNPs for PTC from reference 18 did not replicate (Discussion). Despite sharing the first author and NCI i-Select study platform with shipped row 84 (reference 16, Neta et al., 2011, 10.1093/carcin/bgr100), reference 18 is a separate publication in Laryngoscope reporting distinct 8q24 chromosomal region findings rather than the genomic integrity/HDAC4 findings of reference 16, as the authors themselves distinguish in the quoted sentence.
